theater: 山口萩城與關門海峽一線

battle.name: 第一次長州征討
battle.theater: 山口萩城與關門海峽一線
battle.brief: 一八六四年京都火拼之後，朝廷下勅命討伐長州，幕府自三十五藩調兵十五萬，兵分五道直指山口，卻全未接戰便以切腹斬首收場。卡面這艘一八六二年英國鐵甲艦並未參戰，它代表同年九月下關海峽一役的新世代火力：十七艘木殼軍艦拆掉長州砲台，讓幕府敢屯兵山口，也讓西鄉隆盛在十二月渡海入長府議和。

kit.name: 鐵甲艦
kit.history: 木殼外面包了鐵。裝甲第一次比砲更難對付，砲塔的設計從此繞著它轉。

countries: 交戰的兩方是德川幕府一方與長州藩。幕府一方以將軍德川家茂的名義接下朝廷的勅命，從尾張、越前（福井）以及西國諸藩抽出兵力編成「征長軍」，總督由尾張藩前藩主德川慶勝擔任，副總督由越前藩主松平茂昭擔任，西鄉隆盛以參謀身份加入並實際主持交涉；薩摩藩與筑前藩等九州諸藩亦出兵或居間斡旋，另一端則是京都守護的會津、桑名兩藩與新選組。英國、法國、荷蘭、美國四國聯合艦隊同期在下關海峽砲擊長州藩，雖然不是這場征討的交戰方，卻是幕府敢於集兵的外部前提。長州一方以藩主毛利敬親與其養嗣為名義首腦，萩藩廳的實權派是三名家老家司、益田、福原，外交由吉川經幹主持，武力則是奇兵隊為首的諸隊——遊擊隊、八幡隊、御楯隊、南園隊、力士隊、選鋒隊等藩兵以外的武裝團體，重大決策由諸隊會議合議而定。
countriesEn: The two sides in this war were the Tokugawa shogunate and the Chōshū domain. On the shogunate side the government took up the imperial mandate against Chōshū in the name of the shogun Tokugawa Iesada, drawing contingents from Owari, Echizen (Fukui) and the western domains to form the expeditionary army against Chōshū. The commander-in-chief was Tokugawa Yoshinobu, former lord of Owari, the vice-commander Matsudaira Shigeaki, lord of Echizen, and Saigō Takamori entered as a staff officer and in practice conducted the negotiations; Satsuma and Kyūshū domains such as Chikuzen also sent troops or acted as mediators, while on the other side of the Kyoto confrontation stood Aizu and Kuwana, the Kyoto guard, together with the Shinsengumi. A combined British, French, Dutch and American squadron bombarded Chōshū in the Shimonoseki Strait in the same months; it was not a party to this war, but it was the external premise that allowed the shogunate to mass an army at all. On the Chōshū side the nominal heads were the domain lord Mōri Takachika and his adopted heir, the real power at the Hagi domain office lay with three senior retainers, Kunishi, Masuda and Fukuhara, foreign relations were handled by Kikkawa Tsunemasa, and the armed strength was the Kibintai and the other irregular corps — the Yūgekitai, the Hachiman-tai, the Mitama-tai, the Nanen-tai, the Rikishi-tai and the Senbo-tai — units raised outside the regular domain troops, whose major decisions were taken by a council of the corps' commanders.
people: 這場沒有會戰的戰爭，勝負是由幾個人的判斷與一封信決定的。幕府一方最關鍵的人是西鄉隆盛：他在十月二十四日於大坂向總督慶勝提出以寬典處置長州的方案，慶勝當場把隨身腰刀交給他作為信憑，此後西鄉以參謀格取得全權，十一月四日帶稅所篤、吉井友實進入岩國，與吉川經幹會談，把原本可能開戰的十五萬大軍壓回談判桌；德川慶勝事後又拒絕幕府把藩主父子押送江戶的命令，退居大坂滯坂，替自己留下拒不受命的餘地。長州一方，三名家老家司、益田於德山藩切腹，福原在岩國藩切腹，四名參謀宍戶、竹內、中村、佐久間在野山獄被斬；五条實美等五卿隨後被移交筑前。藩內另一批人走的是相反方向：高杉晉作在十二月十五日夜冒雪赴功山寺集眾起兵，赤禰武人主張調和，山縣有朋以奇兵隊軍監身份遞交反對意見書，井上馨一度被刺客重傷，伊藤博文則出任力士隊總督。
peopleEn: A war without a battle was decided by the judgement of a few men and by a single letter. On the shogunate side the decisive figure was Saigō Takamori: on 24 October he put to the commander-in-chief Yoshinobu at Osaka a plan for handling Chōshū leniently, and Yoshinobu handed him his own short sword on the spot as a pledge of trust; from then on Saigō, who had entered as a staff officer, held full authority, and on 4 November he entered Iwakuni with Saishō Atsushi and Yoshii Tomozane and talked with Kikkawa Tsunemasa, pressing an army of a hundred and fifty thousand men back from the field of battle to the negotiating table. Yoshinobu afterwards refused the order to escort the lord and his heir to Edo and settled in Osaka, keeping open to himself the possibility of refusing further orders. On the Chōshū side three senior retainers, Kunishi and Masuda, committed seppuku at the Tokuyama domain, and Fukuhara at the Iwakuni domain; four staff officers, Shishido, Takeuchi, Nakamura and Sakuma, were beheaded at the No-yama prison; the five court nobles, with Sanjō Sanetomi at their head, were then handed over to Chikuzen. Another group inside the domain went the opposite way: on the night of 15 December Takasugi Shinsaku rode through heavy snow to the Kōzan-ji temple to raise his followers, Akane Takehito argued for reconciliation, Yamagata Yukihiko filed a protest with the Hagi domain office as gunnery officer of the Kibintai, Inoue Kaku was badly wounded by an assassin, and Itō Hirobumi took command of the Rikishi-tai.
kits: 卡面這艘一八六二年式英國鐵甲艦並沒有出現在這場征討的戰場上，但它代表的正是這場征討得以成立的技術前提。一八六四年九月的下關之役，聯合艦隊出動的是木殼軍艦：英方 Euryalus、Conqueror、Tartar、Leopard、Barrosa、Perseus、Argus、Coquette、Bouncer 等九艘，法方 Tancrède、Sémiramis、Dupleix 三艘，荷方 Djambi、Metalen-Kruis、Medusa、Amsterdam 四艘，美方只以一艘租用蒸汽船象徵性同行。真正打掉長州砲台的是後膛砲與射擊紀律，而不是裝甲：前田砲台與壇之浦砲台在兩天內被壓垮，彥島一線繳獲六十門砲，長州藩在海峽裡的蒸汽軍艦 Daniel Webster（六砲）、Lanrick（十砲）、Lancefield（四砲）皆是美國造船，其中兩艘在一八六三年被美艦懷俄明號擊沉、一八六四年又撈起重用。岸上砲台以老舊火砲為主，僅得五門美國贈送的八吋達格倫砲；藩兵的步槍、冷兵與火繩槍同樣過時。幕府征長軍是純粹的陸上兵力，裝備以火繩與洋式步槍、刀槍以及少量新購的小砲為主，可倚靠的洋式火力同樣有限。
kitsEn: The British ironclad of 1862 on this card never fought in this war, but it stands for the technical premise on which the war rested. In the battle of Shimonoseki in September 1864 the allied squadron put to sea wooden warships only: nine British (Euryalus, Conqueror, Tartar, Leopard, Barrosa, Perseus, Argus, Coquette and Bouncer), three French (Tancrède, Sémiramis and Dupleix) and four Dutch (Djambi, Metalen-Kruis, Medusa and Amsterdam), with the Americans represented only by a hired steamer. What actually destroyed the Chōshū batteries was the breech-loading gun and the gunnery, not armour: the Maeda and Tannoura batteries were beaten down within two days, and sixty cannon were captured on the Hikojima line. The Chōshū squadron was three American-built steam warships, the six-gun bark Daniel Webster, the ten-gun brig Lanrick and the four-gun steamer Lancefield, two of which the American sloop Wyoming sank in 1863 and Chōshū raised again in 1864. The shore batteries were manned mostly with antiquated pieces, the only modern armament being five eight-inch Dahlgren guns presented by the United States, while the domain troops carried old muskets, cold weapons and matchlocks. The shogunate army that marched on the domain was a purely land force, equipped with matchlocks and imported muskets, swords, lances and a few newly bought small pieces, with little reliable modern firepower of its own. The point the card makes is a comparative one: in 1864 no ironclad had yet reached the Shimonoseki Strait and the wooden squadron won regardless, which showed that the shell and the gunner, not the armour, then decided such fights; the armoured generation Britain was building in 1862 had not yet entered the reckoning.
tactics: 幕府的戰法是多路合圍加政治收網。八月十三日決定攻勢方向，分芸州口、石州口、大島口、小倉口、萩口五道，目標不是藩主所在的萩城，而是藩主父子所居的山口；總督府設在廣島國泰寺，副總督府設在豐前小倉城，十月二十二日大坂軍議定在十一月十八日開戰。但真正決定戰局的是另一套做法：西鄉把征討的目標從討伐改成請罪，靠薩摩藩士高崎五六與筑前藩士喜多岡勇平先入岩國探路，再以密使穿梭於總督府與萩藩廳之間，兵不血刃地換到家老切腹、參謀斬首、五卿追放與山口城破卻四項條件。與此同時，藩內的諸隊與萩藩廳在山口、萩一帶起了摩擦，十二月下旬至翌年二月在大田、絵堂、呑水峠一線爆發真實的遭遇戰：奇兵隊與御盾隊在川上口的狹窄谷道設成口袋，狙擊隊伏在竹薮，遊擊隊夜襲赤村，用的是町眾與浪人式的散兵、伏擊與夜襲，完全不像徵召制大軍的會戰。
tacticsEn: The shogunate's method was a multi-axis approach closed by political negotiation. On 13 August the lines of advance were fixed at five, Geishū, Sekishū, Ōshima, Kokura and Hagi, and the object was not Hagi castle, where the lord lived, but Yamaguchi, where the lord and his heir were; the headquarters of the commander-in-chief was set up at the Kokutai-ji temple in Hiroshima, the vice-commander's at Kokura castle in Buzen, and a council at Osaka on 22 October set 18 November for the attack to begin. What actually decided the campaign was a different method: Saigō changed the object of the expedition from punitive war to apology, got a foothold in Iwakuni through the Satsuma man Takasaki Goroku and the Chikuzen man Kitaoka Yuhei, and then shuttled between the headquarters and the Hagi domain office, converting a war of a hundred and fifty thousand men into four terms without a shot — the suicide of the three senior retainers, the beheading of the four staff officers, the expulsion of the five court nobles and the demolition of the Yamaguchi works. At the same time the irregular corps and the Hagi domain office came into collision at Yamaguchi and Hagi, and between late December and the following February real skirmishes were fought on the Ōta, E-dō and Nomizu-tōge lines: the Kibintai and the Mitama-tai formed a pocket in the narrow Kawa-kamiguchi defile, marksmen lay in the bamboo clumps, the Yūgekitai attacked Akamura by night, and the whole business was small-arm tactics by townsmen and rōnin, dispersed fire, ambush and night attack, nothing like the set-piece battle of a conscript army.
data: 可以核對的數字大致如下：禁門之變發生在舊曆元治元年七月十九日，即公曆一八六四年八月二十日，長州方投入約三千二百人，幕府一方約六十人死傷，長州方約四百人死傷，十七人切腹；朝廷八月十九日議決討伐，七月二十三日下勅命，正式集兵自公曆八月二十四日起，至舊曆十二月二十七日下解兵令，換算公曆為一八六五年一月二十四日，全程沒有一場正面會戰，兩軍直接戰鬥損失記為零。兵員方面，幕府自三十五至三十六藩徵召，號稱十五萬人；長州藩可調的藩兵與諸隊依記錄為四千人左右或未詳，實際集中於山口與萩的武裝約七百五十人。海上的對照數字是：九月下關一役，聯合艦隊自橫濱出發時為十六艘具名軍艦，另有美方租用蒸汽船隨行，總兵力記為二千人，日方記錄為六艘軍艦、四十艘武裝帆船與約一百門砲；聯軍方面死傷七十二人，日方記為陣亡十八人、受傷二十九人、六十門砲被繳獲，另一份日文記錄把出動船數記為十七艘，砲數為英一六四門、法六十四門、荷五十四門、美四門。錢糧方面，同年下關和約的賠償是三百萬美元，幕府先行支付一百五十萬，其餘由明治政府在一八七四年以後分期償還，美國於一八八三年三月退還其份額七十八萬五千零八十七美元又八十七分。交涉與處置的時間點也有記錄：十月二十二日大坂軍議，十一月四日西鄉入岩國，十一月十一日與十二日三名家老切腹、四參謀斬首，十一月十六日廣島首實檢，十一月十八日降伏命令，十二月五日謝罪文書，十二月十一日西鄉渡海入長府，十二月十五日功山寺起兵。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. The clash at the Hamaguri Gate took place on the nineteenth day of the seventh month of the first year of Genji, that is 20 August 1864 by the Gregorian calendar; Chōshū put about 3,200 men into it, the shogunate side lost about sixty men and Chōshū about four hundred, and seventeen men committed suicide. The court resolved to punish Chōshū on 19 August, the mandate was issued on the twenty-third, the mustering began on 24 August, and the order to disband the expeditionary army came on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month, which is 24 January 1865; there was not a single pitched engagement in between, and the direct combat losses of both sides are recorded as nil. On numbers of men, the shogunate drew contingents from thirty-five to thirty-six domains and claimed a hundred and fifty thousand; the fighting men Chōshū could raise are given as around four thousand or as unknown, and the irregular corps actually concentrated at Yamaguchi and Hagi numbered about seven hundred and fifty. The naval comparison for the same year runs as follows: the allied squadron that steamed out of Yokohama in late August was made up of sixteen named warships, with a hired steamer in token American attendance, and about two thousand soldiers, marines and sailors; Chōshū was credited with six warships, forty war-junks and roughly one hundred cannon; the allies lost seventy-two killed and wounded, and the Japanese account gives eighteen killed, twenty-nine wounded and sixty cannon captured, while another Japanese record gives the sailing force as seventeen ships carrying 164 British, 64 French, 54 Dutch and 4 American guns. On money, the indemnity of the Shimonoseki accord was three million dollars, of which the shogunate paid one and a half million in advance and the remainder was repaid by the Meiji government in instalments from 1874; in March 1883 the United States returned its share of 785,000 dollars and 87 cents. The sequence of the negotiations is also recorded: the council at Osaka on 22 October, Saigō's entry into Iwakuni on 4 November, the suicides of the three senior retainers and the beheading of the four staff officers on the eleventh and twelfth, the inspection at Hiroshima on the sixteenth, the terms of surrender on the eighteenth, the written apology on 5 December, Saigō's crossing of the strait to Nagato on the eleventh, and the rising at Kōzan-ji on the fifteenth.
cause: 起因是公曆一八六四年八月二十日京都蛤御門前的一場火拼。長州藩以「藩主冤罪向帝申訴」的名義分三路入京：國司親相與來島又兵衛屯天龍寺，真木保臣與久坂玄瑞在山崎與天王山，福原元僴在伏見；會津、桑名、越前、彥根與薩摩各藩以及新選組在御所前堵住他們，來島與久坂重傷切腹，福原在伏見兵敗。更深的一層是「尊王攘夷」旗號下的困局：一八六三年五月十日長州藩炮擊美國商船 Pembroke，五月二十三日傷法國通報艦 Kien-Chang，五月二十六日再攻荷蘭 Medusa，六月一日美軍懷俄明號擊沉其蒸汽軍艦兩艘，六月五日法軍以 Tancrède 與 Sémiramis 砲擊前田與壇之浦砲台，海峽自此封鎖；同一批人在京都又打著天皇旗號砲擊皇宮，於是既傷了洋人又傷了朝廷。八月十八日政變後長州勢力被逐出京都，池田屋事件中藩士又被新選組殺傷，兩面受敵之下，藩主父子只能靠出兵的說法去堵京城的非難，這一舉措把藩內的爭執推成了國家層面的朝敵問題，幕府也才有理由調動三十五藩的大軍。
causeEn: The cause was a firefight before the Hamaguri Gate in Kyoto on 20 August 1864. Chōshū advanced on Kyoto in three columns under the slogan of the lord's grievance being put to the emperor: Kunishi and Kijima with a force at Tenryū-ji, Maki and Kusaka at Yamazaki and Tennōzan, and Fukuhara at Fushimi; Aizu, Kuwana, Echizen, Hikone and Satsuma, with the Shinsengumi, blocked them before the palace, Kijima and Kusaka were wounded and committed suicide, and Fukuhara was beaten at Fushimi. Beneath that lay the trap of the banner of reverence for the emperor and expulsion of the foreigners. On 10 May 1863 Chōshū fired on the American merchant steamer Pembroke, damaged the French dispatch vessel Kien Chan on the twenty-third, attacked the Dutch Medusa on the twenty-sixth, and on 1 June the American sloop Wyoming sank two of the Chōshū steamers; on 5 June the French Tancrède and Sémiramis bombarded the Maeda and Tannoura batteries, and from that day the strait was closed. The same men who fired on the foreign shipping then fired on the imperial palace in Kyoto under the emperor's own flag, so that they had now offended the foreigners and the court at once. After the coup of 18 August Chōshū was driven out of Kyoto, and in the Ikedaya affair its men were killed by the Shinsengumi. Caught between the two, the lord and his heir could only answer the capital's charges by marching on the capital, and that single gesture turned a dispute inside the domain into a matter of state in which Chōshū was made an enemy of the throne, which in turn gave the shogunate the pretext to mobilise the armies of thirty-five domains.
impact: 這場征討的後果不在戰場而在政局。表面上幕府以零戰鬥的代價拿到一次漂亮的處置：藩主父子請罪、三名家老切腹、五卿放逐、山口城破卻，幕府威信似是重振。但同一件事也把長州藩劈成兩半：正義派與俗論黨在萩藩廳得勢，倒幕派則在十二月十五日功山寺一聚另起爐灶，元治二年初的絵堂、大田、呑水峠一役之後俗論黨崩潰，高杉晉作、山縣有朋一系掌握了藩政，並以此為核心推動薩長同盟。另一方面，幕府要靠三十五藩的兵與外國艦隊的壓力才得以行事，反而向天下顯示了幕府對諸藩的支配並不牢固，兩年後第二次長州征討便因薩摩不出一兵而打了個空，幕府第二次敗北，連帶大政奉還，最後走到王政復古。錢上的尾巴拖得更長：三百萬美元的賠償讓幕府無法一次付清，東京政府在一八七四年後以分期方式償還，美國於一八八三年退還其份額，該款後來成為擴建橫濱港的資金來源之一，一八九六年完工。
impactEn: The consequences of this war lie in politics, not on the battlefield. On the face of it the shogunate bought a handsome settlement at the price of no battle at all: the apology of the lord and his heir, the suicide of the three senior retainers, the expulsion of the five court nobles and the demolition of the Yamaguchi works, and the authority of the shogunate seemed to be restored. But the same event split the Chōshū domain in two. The righteous faction and the commoners' party held the Hagi domain office, while the anti-shogunate faction struck out on its own at the gathering at Kōzan-ji on 15 December; after the fighting at E-dō, Ōta and Nomizu-tōge in the first months of the following year the commoners' party collapsed, and Takasugi Shinsaku and Yamagata Yukihiko took control of the domain and made the Satsuma-Chōshū alliance the core of what followed. On the other side, the fact that the shogunate could act only by means of the contingents of thirty-five domains and the pressure of foreign squadrons showed to the whole country that its hold over the domains was not secure. Two years later the Second Chōshū Expedition went nowhere because Satsuma would not send a single man, the shogunate was defeated for the second time, and the transfer of authority followed, and with it the restoration of imperial rule. The financial tail was longer still: three million dollars of indemnity was more than the shogunate could pay at once, the Tokyo government repaid it in instalments after 1874, the United States returned its share in 1883, and that money later became one of the sources for the enlargement of Yokohama harbour, completed in 1896.
result: 結果是一場以認罪收尾的戰爭。長州藩交出藩主父子的謝罪文書，接受家老切腹、參謀斬首、五卿移交筑前、山口城（實為山城館）破卻四項條件；幕府軍在舊曆十二月十七日下解兵令，總督德川慶勝把處分權交回幕府後，又拒絕把藩主父子押送江戶的命令，退居大坂滯坂，二月朝廷要求上洛他也不去。雙方都沒有得到想要的東西：幕府拿到了形式上的勝利，卻在藩內埋下倒幕派的種子；長州藩保住性命，卻被切斷了正義派的路。真正的結局在半年之後：功山寺起兵與元治內亂讓倒幕派掌權，第二次長州征討幕府一敗塗地，德川慶喜接任將軍並提出大政奉還，一八六七年十二月王政復古，江戶幕府就此結束。而卡面這艘鐵甲艦所代表的技術轉折，則在這條鏈條的另一端：下關海峽的砲火讓長州藩的海岸線從此無險，幕府的西式軍隊得以用槍砲與後膛砲壓過刀劍之類的舊戰法，倒幕的勝負最後是在這套新技術加新財政的底子上才分出來的。
resultEn: The result was a war that ended in an apology. Chōshū handed over the written apology of the lord and his heir and accepted the four terms: the suicide of the three senior retainers, the beheading of the four staff officers, the transfer of the five court nobles to Chikuzen and the demolition of the Yamaguchi works, which was in fact a mansion rather than a castle. The expeditionary army was ordered to disband on the seventeenth day of the twelfth month; the commander-in-chief Tokugawa Yoshinobu handed the power of punishment back to the shogunate and then refused the order to escort the lord and his heir to Edo, settling in Osaka and declining to go up to Kyoto in February. Neither side got what it wanted: the shogunate had a formal victory and sowed the seed of the anti-shogunate faction inside the domain; Chōshū saved its life and lost the righteous party's road. The real ending came half a year later: the rising at Kōzan-ji and the civil war of the first year of Genji put the anti-shogunate faction in power, the shogunate was crushed in the Second Chōshū Expedition, Tokugawa Yoshinobu succeeded as shogun and proposed the transfer of authority, and in December 1867 the imperial restoration ended the Tokugawa shogunate. The technical turning point that the ironclad on this card stands for lies at the other end of the same chain: the gunfire in the Shimonoseki Strait left the Chōshū coast without a natural defence, the shogunate's Western-trained troops could beat cold steel with muskets and breech-loading guns, and in the end the struggle for power was decided on the base of that new technology and that new money.
